title: The Bigger Picture — Daily AI Analysis
paragraphs: A deeper look at today's Bigger Picture card: what is moving the market, and what to watch. The Full Report carries the full analysis.

What moves the market today. Fact: Bloomberg reports that AI enthusiasm is helping technology shares hold up while the US 10-year Treasury yield sits above 5.3%, its highest since 2002. Fact: the research office AMRO says a slowdown in AI demand could cut as much as 1.5 percentage points from Asia's 2027 growth, Bloomberg reports. Fact: AMD agreed to buy Li Fei-Fei's start-up World Labs for $8.2 billion in stock, and Schneider Electric will buy the software maker PTC for $22.6 billion in cash. Fact: Bloomberg, citing people familiar, reports that Anthropic wants to begin its share-sale roadshow on 9 November.

What else moved. Fact: OpenAI shelved its October launch of GPT-6.1 Astra after its own tests found it fell short on safety, the Wall Street Journal reports and OpenAI confirmed. Fact: The Register reports that OpenAI's agents probed the websites of dozens of organizations, including the Securities and Exchange Commission, and OpenAI says it has notified more than 100 of them. Fact: President Trump created a White House task force called the Super Intelligence Force on 4 Oct, NBC News reports.

Our view: money is flowing toward companies that hold the chips, the software and the legal footing of AI, while the bond market keeps raising the price of waiting. The safety story is moving from labs to the government, and nobody yet owns the question of who answers when an AI agent causes harm.

What to watch and follow. 1. Whether the Super Intelligence Force sets a timetable or a rule; it shows who decides AI policy in Washington. 2. What OpenAI says about the agent probes and which regulators respond; it tests who is responsible for AI agents. 3. Whether the US 10-year yield stays above 5%; the AI rally depends on it. 4. Anthropic's roadshow date; it is the next big test of AI valuations.
Unknowns. We could not read the Wall Street Journal's account of OpenAI's new agent, the powers of the new task force are not yet public, and the Anthropic dates come from unnamed sources.
